title: Johan Banér to Torsten Stålhandske, Hof, 29 December 1640: intercepted copy in Kircher's correspondence (APUG 568 f. 239), posted unsolved on Cipherbrain 2019

documents.shelfmark: Archivio della Pontificia Università Gregoriana, APUG 568 f. 239r-v (Kircher correspondence); images as posted on Cipherbrain, 2 June 2019
documents.route: Johan Banér (Hof, Upper Franconia) to Major General Torsten Stålhandske (Silesia); intercepted, copy

plaintext.source: No decipherment with the copy as posted; none found in print or online (Cipherbrain comments 2019-2020: attempts failed).

transcription.source: Philip Neal's transcription (Cipherbrain), checked figure by figure against the Museo Galileo scans of APUG 568 f. 239r-v (1469x2304 px)
transcription.notes: 274 two-digit values and 14 three-digit code words (--drop-first). Four figures corrected from the scans: S4 66->86, S4 36->86, S5 57->47, S7 illegible->92.

system.summary: Two-digit homophonic alphabet (1-6 values per letter, 2-98) inside clear German, with three-digit code words (361-568 names and nouns, 766-783 short words or syllables).
system.notes: Not banded like the Swedish chancery keys of 1634-40 on DECODE (R4123, R4325), and not any of the Banér keys there. The 7xx codes sit where the dropped letters of darau(ff), au(ss), ko(mm)en fall; they may be syllable or double-letter codes.

prior_solution.where: Cipherbrain post 2 June 2019 and comments (Neal, SantaColoma) report failed attempts; DECODE has no record of the letter; web search 22 Sept 2026 found no reading.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: DECODE API scan of Riksarkivet Chifferklaver box II

solution.what: Fetched the Cipherbrain post (2 June 2019): two page images, Neal's transcription, the comments. Identified '568 239r' as APUG 568 (Kircher correspondence); the Museo Galileo image database needs a registered login; EMLO has no record.

Took Neal's transcription into ct_neal.txt as seven segments S1-S7 (274 two-digit values, 74 distinct; 14 three-digit codes); checked it against the blog images, which are too small to confirm single figures.
Unconstrained homophonic annealing with the de-1500s 5-gram model: overfits to en/ne/sie strings.
Crib 'auf den [442]' before 'loszugehen': produces 'due' elsewhere; dropped.

Scanned the Riksarkivet key box (Chifferklaver låda II, DECODE R4103-R4329) through the API and the archivists' cover labels; transcribed and tried the Banér keys R4122 (Horn-Banér), R4123 (Banér 1634, = R4325 'Generalis Campi Marschalli Johan Banneris Cyffer'), R4325's other alphabets and R4266, as is and with value offsets -30..+30.

From the Swedish keys: values in four bands, each band a permutation of the alphabet. Banded swap annealer (solve3.py) recovers a synthetic control enciphered with R4123 when given about 8 crib values; on the letter no band layout scores near a true solution.

Synthetic control (1630s German from Theatrum Europaeum, same segment lengths, R4123 key): true plaintext scores -279 against -390..-430 for unconstrained optima, so the search needs cribs; with 8 crib values a multiset model (4 homophones per letter, no bands) reaches -275.
S6 opens after 'mich aber von zeit zu zeit' with 40 16 23 28 29 = durch; 16 64 40 = und. With these fixed the multiset annealer produced 'nach der ... pfaltz und' in S3.
S3 = 'nach der Oberpfaltz und gegen die [442]' (Banér's march from Hof into the Upper Palatinate towards Regensburg): 20 values fixed, all consistent with durch/und.

Key extended word by word from the context and cross-checked across segments: Schlesien agirende, dazu ziehen, etwa auch (S4); gute acht geben, sobaldt, ehender, solche, Fürsichtigkeit nachvolgen (S5); wohin er seine(n) Marche zu richte(n) entgegen (S7); Johann, über (S2). 70 values in key.json.
decode.py applies key.json: 239 of 274 cipher tokens read as sense (87.2%); unread: a name in S2, 14 tokens in S5, 4 tokens in S1, 2 in S6, the illegible figure in S7; all 14 code words open.
Found the Museo Galileo Kircher scans served openly (archimede.imss.fi.it/kircher/568/large/239r.jpg, 239v.jpg); the login only guards the search database.
Re-read every cipher line on the scans: Neal right except four figures (S4 66->86, 36->86; S5 57->47; S7 = 92).

Re-measured with the corrected transcription: 244 of 274 (89.1%); S1 = Jobs[508] (Jobst), S7 complete. Digit-confusion search (emend.py) finds nothing for the S5 stretch; the copy itself is corrupt there.

Freed every value in the unread stretches and treated the 7xx codes as letters: the annealer returned 'auf solche Weise' (772 f, 766 W) and 'dass sie mögen' (783 g, 60 m) unprompted; 246 of 274 (89.8%). All three-digit numbers as letters does not read.

outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py over ct_neal.txt (corrected against the APUG 568 scans): two-digit cipher tokens in words read as sense, 246/274; code words excluded

gaps.detail: Figures confirmed on the manuscript scan; values fixed elsewhere, so the only known copy is corrupt; the sent original or a Swedish register copy is not digitised.

gaps.item: S5 'eisen o vi rechte' (14), 'o ?' (2), stray e (1)
gaps.detail: Figures confirmed on the manuscript scan; the copy is corrupt; another witness needed.
No key survives; each occurs once. 766, 770, 772, 778, 783 read as letters.

outcome.notes: First reading of the letter. Key rebuilt here from context cribs; no Swedish key on DECODE matches.
